blocks.name: register_file
blocks.responsibility: Implement 32 32-bit integer registers with asynchronous reads, synchronous writes, asynchronous active-high reset, hardwired-zero x0, and ignored writes to x0.
blocks.design_rationale: Separating architectural state makes reset behavior, x0 handling, and register read/write timing easy to verify without adding cycles to the single-cycle datapath.

blocks.name: alu
blocks.responsibility: Decode opcode, funct3, and funct7 to perform RV32I integer and address arithmetic, shifts, signed and unsigned comparisons, branch-condition evaluation, and all RV32M multiplication, division, and remainder operations, including defined divide-by-zero and signed-overflow results.
blocks.design_rationale: A combinational ALU keeps arithmetic and RV32M behavior in one independently testable block, while combinational results preserve one-instruction-per-cycle execution.

blocks.name: cpu
blocks.responsibility: Implement the exact external CPU bus contract and single-cycle control. Maintain the PC; decode instructions and form I, S, B, U, and J immediates; select operands; instantiate the register_file and alu; implement LUI, AUIPC, JAL, JALR, and conditional branches; calculate byte-addressed load/store addresses; drive store width, data, and write enable; select and extend load data according to width, address offset, and signedness; select register writeback data; and advance the PC with the specified priority. Reset the PC asynchronously to zero.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeping instruction decode, PC control, and memory-bus formatting at the top level makes the externally observable contract straightforward to verify; the two combinational datapath blocks avoid extra execution cycles.

notes: Use only ieee.std_logic_1164 and ieee.numeric_std. The cpu entity has exactly the specified ports and no generics. All combinational outputs must have defaults, and each signal must have a single driver.
